chunks: And if one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him asylum so that he may hear the word of God. Then escort him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.

key_terms.قَوْمٌ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ: a people who do not know

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for granting asylum to a polytheist who seeks protection?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this verse establishes the *ijarah* (asylum) contract as a binding obligation, requiring the Muslim to ensure the polytheist not only hears the Quran but also receives a secure escort to their destination. Scholars emphasize that the phrase 'until he hears the word of Allah' implies a duty to convey the message clearly, while the reason 'because they are a people who do not know' underscores that ignorance, not hostility, is the primary context for this mercy. This ruling serves as a foundational precedent for diplomatic immunity and the protection of non-Muslims in Islamic statecraft.
